guidance.summary: Meta guides Q4 2026 revenue of $73-76 billion, raises its 2026 total expense outlook to $175-179 billion to include the legal charge, narrows 2026 capex to $135-145 billion, expects Reality Labs losses of $18-19 billion in 2026 narrowing to around $15 billion in 2027, and anticipates strong revenue growth and continued aggressive investment in 2027.

guidance.sentence: We expect fourth quarter 2026 total revenue to be in the range of $73-76 billion.
We now expect full year 2026 total expenses to be in the range of $175-179 billion.
Excluding the third quarter legal charge, we continue to expect 2026 operating income to be above 2025 operating income.
At a segment level, we now expect Reality Labs losses to decline compared to 2025 to a range of $18-19 billion.
We anticipate 2026 capital expenditures, including principal payments on finance leases, to be in the range of $135-145 billion, narrowed from our prior outlook of $130-145 billion.
Absent any changes to our tax landscape, we expect our fourth quarter 2026 tax rate to be between 15-17%.

Looking beyond 2026, we are still developing our budget and capacity plans for next year, but we expect to continue investing aggressively to support both our core business and emerging AI initiatives.

Looking ahead, although we are not providing a full-year 2027 revenue outlook, the benefits our AI investments are delivering to the core business, combined with emerging opportunities from model advances and product launches, position us to sustain strong overall revenue growth throughout 2027.

Separately, we remain focused on improving Reality Labs profitability and expect losses to narrow next year to around $15 billion as we reallocate investment toward other priority areas, primarily AI.

sentences: Our guidance assumes foreign currency is an approximately 1% headwind to year-over-year total revenue growth, based on current exchange rates.

writeup.headline: Meta rates Hold: strong growth and balance sheet offset by a weak trend, legal overhang and a high P/FCF.
writeup.thesis: Meta scores 57, a Hold, because strong fundamentals are balanced by weak price action and valuation. Growth is solid, with TTM revenue growth of 27.5% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 26.1% year on year, though growth slowed by 1.9 pp from the previous quarter. Quality is high, with an 81.0% gross margin and a 32.9% operating margin, and the balance sheet scores 91 with net debt at 0.04 times FCF. Valuation scores only 33. In absolute terms the multiples are high, with P/FCF of 55.0 and an FCF yield 3.2 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield, because heavy capex keeps the FCF margin at 11.9%. Against its own history, P/S and EV/EBIT sit near the middle, while P/FCF is more expensive than at 60 of the last 61 month-ends. The trend score of 30 and a news score of 51, pulled down by a $25B New Mexico privacy penalty, keep the stock out of Buy territory.
key_risks: Litigation and regulation: a $25B New Mexico privacy penalty under appeal, plus a large Q3 legal charge tied to the state attorneys general settlement.
Heavy spending: 2026 capex of $135-145 billion and total expenses raised to $175-179 billion, which squeezes free cash flow.
Reality Labs losses expected at $18-19 billion in 2026.
Weak momentum: price 21.2% below its 52-week high and shares 17.4 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days.
what_would_change: Up to Buy (8 points needed): a recovery in the trend factor, for example the price moving back above its 50-day and 200-day averages.
Up: a better valuation score if free cash flow grows faster than the share price, lowering P/FCF from 55.0.
Down to Sell (13 points of room): a sharp growth slowdown alongside further legal setbacks or a lost appeal on the $25B penalty.
Down: capex guidance rising further and eroding the FCF margin and the quality score.
